memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The next day he went out and saw two Hebrews fighting. He asked the one in the wrong, "Why are you hitting your fellow Hebrew?" The man said, "Who made you ruler and judge over us? Are you thinking of killing me as you killed the Egyptian?" Then Moses was afraid and thought, "What I did must have become known."" - Exodus 2:13-14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses tries again, this time as a peacemaker between two of his own people. And he is thrown back on his heels: Who made you ruler and judge over us?

It is a bitter moment. The man he was trying to help refuses his authority and exposes his sin in the same breath. Moses' whole self-appointed mission collapses in one sentence.

Stephen would later quote this very rejection when he preached (Acts 7:35), and his point was sharp: Israel rejected the deliverer God had sent. It would happen again. Jesus came to His own, and His own did not receive Him (Jn 1:11), and men asked Him too by what authority He acted.

There is also honest comfort here for us. Sometimes we try to help and get rejected. Sometimes our own past is thrown in our face. It does not mean God is finished with us. Moses' story is not over — it is barely beginning.

But notice the last line: Moses was afraid. The man who buried a body now discovers that sin does not stay buried.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How do I respond when my attempt to help is thrown back at me?
2. Is there something hidden in my life that I need to bring into God's light?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I bring my hidden failures to You rather than burying them. Thank You that Your grace is greater than my past. Amen.
